prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Make ONE transparent 2D game obstacle for a 120x120 wu test map. FIRST image is its unique fixed footprint mask: preserve its boundary, proportions and orientation. SECOND image is the SMALL sprite used as a shared visual style and detail-scale reference. Content: pale cracked royal limestone with ice-blue and warm-gold protective circuits. The NEW footprint measures 24.77 by 19.40 world units. CRITICAL: the whole footprint is larger, but individual objects remain at the SAME WORLD SCALE as on small footprints. Gold/blue circuit 0.12 wu thick. EVERY glowing diamond, including the central diamond, 0.65 wu across maximum. Limestone slabs 0.8-1.4 wu. No giant central emblem or oversized medallion. Repeat small motifs across large areas. Infer pixel sizes as feature-world-size / footprint-world-size; for example a 0.65 wu diamond is only 2.6% of this footprint's width. Cover large areas by adding more same-sized elements and terrain, never by enlarging a copied miniature. Preserve angled top-down perspective, painterly matte storybook palette, deep plum outer contour. All ground-level; human pursuers cross while player is excluded. Transparent outside mask, no exterior glow/vignette/shadow, no walls, buildings, people or text. Across this large footprint use at least 70 small limestone slabs and 10-15 SMALL diamond nodes. NO giant central medallion. Each diamond is 3 percent of total footprint width or less.
constraints: fixed authored orientation and footprint size; no random rotation or scale
